content.thinking:
I'm planning the whole scene in one pass: a sturdy workbench with legs, drawer, and under-shelf, topped with alchemy props like glowing potion bottles, stacked books, a balance scale, herb bundles, mortar and pestle, an alembic, a candle, and a scroll.

I'm mapping out the imports and helper functions I'll need—box and lathe builders for geometry, plus a bottle helper that constructs glass and liquid shapes using lathe outlines for the potion containers.

Since transparency isn't supported, I'll fake the glass look by making the liquid body itself the glowing colored part, with a pale glass neck, cork, and a label plane rendered from an SVG texture facing forward.

Now I'm laying out the table: a wood-grain painted top slab around y=0.87-0.9, four legs, a back shelf unit, and a lower shelf at y=0.25 holding crates, a bucket, and sacks for set dressing.

I'm adding drawer fronts with gold knobs and gold trim strips along the table edges, then building a back hutch with a panel, uprights, a shelf of jars, and a top rail hung with herb bundles—cards oriented to hang upward with a 180 lean. On the right side I'm placing a balance scale with a post, crossbar beam, chains, and pans, plus starting a stack of books nearby.

For the left side at x=-0.6, I'm laying out color-varied boxes with cream inset page edges and gold bands, plus an open book made of two tilted page slabs with rune decals lying flat. I'm also planning a mortar and pestle, an alembic with a glowing flask and swept neck tube, and a candle with a glowing flame cone.

Now I'm adding glowing crystal clusters using icosahedron geometry, mushroom pots, and herb plant pots, plus bunches of leaf-textured herb cards leaning at small random angles across the table. I'm also designing hanging tassels with gold cords near the shelf edge and a crimson cloth table runner with gold trim and a patterned decal underneath the items.

Setting the table surface height to 0.9, with the slab centered at 0.87 and legs reaching down to 0.84, then defining the color palette—wood tones, gold, cream, teal, purple, pink, amber, and green—to use throughout the scene.

Writing helper functions...

Still shaping bottle geometry...

Lathe facing details are minor. For wood grain painting, the box parts can reuse the position-based paint function fine. I'm now planning the hanging herb rack with a rod and bundles, plus the hutch shelf items -- jars, books, and a glowing orb with a gold torus ring.

For the back panel, I'm adding a decal with an alchemic circle in gold lines, transparent so the panel shows through, positioned just in front of the panel surface. I'm working out exact depths so the hutch shelf and panel face align correctly, then planning gold star accents.

Now I'm defining a lathed scale-pan shape using a non-crossing outline profile, then building the scale structure itself with a base disk, support post, and finial on top.

For the balance beam, I'm adding a horizontal rod with gold pans suspended by three chains each from the beam ends, placing a weight on one side and a glowing gem on the other, plus a pointer rod hanging down with a dial plate. Now I'm starting a lathed mortar bowl shape positioned off to the side.

Still positioning the alembic setup...

For each book I'm layering thin top/bottom cover boards with a spine strip on the back edge, leaving the cream pages box visible on the front and sides so it reads as a closed book rather than a solid block.

I'll keep the pages flat with a centered ridge spine and add decal text planes, cover boards, and a gold ribbon bookmark hanging down. For the crystal cluster, I'm making glowing six-sided cones as spikes mounted on a grey-blue dodecahedron rock base, placed on the table's right-back area.

Next I'm adding a clay pot with a circular arrangement of herb cards leaning outward radially from the center, tilted about 35 degrees, plus a drawer front with apron boxes beneath the tabletop.

Between the legs I'm placing three drawer faces with gold knob spheres and a keyhole escutcheon, plus a painted apron panel. Below that, a lower shelf holds a barrel with bands, a tied sack, a crate, a bucket, and a cluster of glowing potions. I'm also adding decorative gold tassels hanging from the table's front corners and the shelf edge, each with a cord, knot sphere, and red-and-gold cone tassel.

Now I'm building up the hutch structure itself: a crown rail with gold trim and roof overhang near the top, finial spheres on the uprights, and side posts framing the hutch. I'm adjusting the shelf and herb-rod heights so hanging herb bundles don't overlap the items sitting on the shelf below, settling on a shelf around y=1.2 and a herb rod higher up with shorter hanging bundles to keep clearance.

I'm separating the hanging bundle positions and shelf-item positions by x-coordinate so they don't visually collide, deciding to skip a central hanging lantern in favor of simple glow orbs placed on the shelf instead. Now I'm sketching out the SVG textures needed -- a leafy stem texture in two greens, and a lavender sprig with purple dots along the stem -- before moving on to designing the card elements.

Writing SVG textures...

I'm also thinking through TypeScript typing concerns, like making sure rotation values match the expected vector array type and checking that the frame module's exports are compatible with how I'm calling it for the card layout.

Setting up wood grain paint colors for horizontal and vertical board textures...

Now I need a yaw rotation helper to compute rotated offsets for book boxes placed at an angle, then start writing the book-generating function with position, size, and color parameters.

Working out book geometry: pages, spine, and boards as separate boxes with slightly offset sizes so the spine sits flush against the pages, carefully adjusting the depth offsets so nothing overlaps or leaves gaps.

Defining potion bottle shapes...

Still working out the rings, labels, and torus orientation details, then I need to add helpers for cards and crystal shapes before assembling the full scene.

Writing cards config...

For hanging bundles I'm planning frames anchored at rod points, with downward lean and flow pointing along z, using cross-sections and varied sizes per strand.
